changes.title: `docair explain` now writes a review: the AI groups the changed pieces into changes, one difference in what the app does each, and the changes page leads with that review.

how.words: Finds the pieces of the whole change once, across every flow, instead of per flow.
Collects the commit messages and changed docs between the two versions for the review.
Shapes a commit message for the AI to read, as a source it may cite.
Shapes a changed Markdown file for the AI to read, as a source it may cite.
Shapes a doc block whose words changed, showing its summary before and after.
Caps how much of a commit message body goes to the AI.
Caps how many changed lines of one Markdown file go to the AI.
Caps how many changed lines of all Markdown files together go to the AI.
Builds the compact picture of the pieces for the model.
The request that asks the model to group the pieces into changes with what, how, why, check and disagreements.
Holds which pieces the AI put into one change.
Checks the AI's claims against both graphs, the pieces and the sources it may cite.
Names a piece so the AI's answer can be bound back to it.
Shows one piece of a change in the order the change's pieces work together.
Names a piece's new, gone and edited parts in a few words for the reader.
Runs the review with a given model answer, binding and storing it.
Runs `docair explain` end to end: pieces, intent, model, bound review.
Reports progress of the review on stderr.
Shows the review on the page: the AI's changes in its order, each at `#review/<n>` on its own picture.
The page component that leads the changes list with the review, each change's details and pictures.
A change's details now draw from the review instead of the old recorded per-flow findings.
Tests that a reviewed change leads the list, opens on its own picture with its why and the other edits.
Holds the changed `docair explain` tests.
Holds the changed changes-page tests.
The commits module gained the intent gathering.
The project server runs the new review job.

changes.why: A reviewer reviews changes, not flows: before, the changes section listed 31 flows and a new peer showed up in 16 of them, so docair now finds the pieces once and the AI groups them into changes as the reader understands them, with every claim bound and every leftover piece shown as an other edit.
changes.check: The AI's grouping is model output: check that every piece is covered by a change or listed as an other edit, and that cited sources really say what the why claims.

changes.title: A big flow's changes section now shows one picture per change, with everything not relevant folded away, instead of one huge picture.

how.words: The threshold above which a flow's picture switches to one picture per change.
Back and Next links between the per-change pictures.
Says where a step's picture stands among the flow's pictures: its place and how many.
Back and Next of step k of n as the walk goes through the pictures.
The change details link to the folded whole-flow and all-changes views.
The diff module's fingerprint rework sits beside this change.

changes.why: A picture of more than 30 parts is too big to find its changes in: on docair's own work, *Datum graph* had 182 parts and 45 changes, so each change now gets its own picture with the rest folded away.
changes.check: Folding must not lose lines: check that a line whose end is folded into a closed box still points at that box, one per pair.

changes.title: The diff no longer marks untouched bodies as edited: a part that kept its id counts as changed only when its text really differs.

how.words: One fingerprint hash that leaves out the graph's part names, used to find moves and renames.
The second hash, of every word: the same text is the same body whatever the graph calls things.

changes.why: Before, the diff called untouched bodies edited, so callers of a renamed part or text that merely moved showed up as changes.
changes.check: Check that a genuinely edited body is still caught: it must differ in both hashes, so an edit that only renames graph parts would now read as unchanged.

changes.title: Asking the model now can skip deep reasoning: with `think` false the request sets `reasoning_effort: low`.

how.words: The plain chat path, whose direct calls to post, error handling and endpoint moved into `chat_with`.

changes.why: The review asks the model to reason little first, per the commit message.
changes.check: Check that `think` true still gets full reasoning, and that the low-effort setting does not weaken the binding of the review's claims.
